name: plan-china-high-council
description: The Chinese High Council (0.8.4): an alternative route next to the three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council), not a replacement for any of them, with the shape of plan-high-council. It runs the planning stages with three proposers (Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) and a layered review panel of eight named judges in three layers: layer 1 GLM-5.3 Flash, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash; layer 2 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3, Qwen 3.8 27B; layer 3 Kimi K3.1 Pro and Qwen 3.8 Max. Each seat carries a persona name in the form title (seat_personas), which is the title of the seat and changes nothing the seat does. Every proposer and judge is a model from a Chinese lab. Exactly these eight judge seats vote; they are filled by eight models from five companies, and the review panel counts eight labs, one per model. Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain runs the ladder (its ladder key: block 3, visits 3): layer 1 revises in blocks of 3, then layer 2 is asked (up to 3 visits), then layer 3 reads; each layer-3 visit is one top-layer read. It has no round limit: the run ends on agreement, on a stall the top layer holds, at the limit you type (--rounds counts top-layer reads) or when you stop it. When a stall at the top layer, a judge that stays silent after its solo ask, or your own stop ends the work for now, the run is stopped, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose how to go on: continue, finish at once, finish after one last top-layer read, or revise the draft yourself; the run's spending limit still applies. On a ladder run the plan is never sent up a layer ahead of its turn: each layer is asked when the ladder's order reaches it. answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria stage is answered through your Claude subscription (the Opus 5.5 seat, `provider: external`). The skeleton, build, revise, handoff and decider stages are answered by your Claude Code session (`provider: external`). A stage that waits for an external answer pauses the run with exit code 3 until it is answered. These Claude-backed stages are the only exceptions to the Chinese-model roster. This chain needs the zero-data-retention setting of your OpenRouter account switched off: Qwen 3.8 Flash and Qwen 3.8 Max are served only by Alibaba hosts, none of them on OpenRouter's zero-data-retention list, so with that setting on there is no host for those two seats and the run stops at their first call (a judge is never skipped). A chain cannot switch the setting off for you: OpenRouter does not let a request override an account-wide zero-data-retention setting. Every API seat reasons at high, except Qwen 3.8 27B, which runs at xhigh because the model offers no high setting (the chain states xhigh for it); no Grok, no Mistral. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3 Flash, Qwen 3.8 Flash and Qwen 3.8 Max 131,072; Qwen 3.8 27B 128,000 (the maintainer's choice; the lab's own figure is 131,072). For Kimi K3.1 Pro and MiniMax M3.1 Flash no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Dry run (0.8.4, prices of 2026-11-11, the dry run's assumed sizes): $14.88 expected (3 top-layer reads, the read that signs off counted, each after a climb of about 8 layer-1 passes and 1 layer-2 pass: the average of one measured run) and an upper estimate of $464.22 (7 top-layer reads, an assumption, each with the full ladder below it), about $14.88 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate counts the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat) and the solo ask of a silent judge at the review's expected cost, but leaves out answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($464.22) and the expected figure ($14.88) are above the default cap of $12, the figure the dry run compares a chain with; the cheapest end ($9.20, one overseer round, the dry run's floor) fits under it. On the command line your limit is the number you type. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $12 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default a run that uses its whole allowance stops at the ceiling (the upper estimate and the expected figure are above it; the cheapest end, $9.20, fits under it). This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run.
summary: Eight judges and three proposers, all Chinese labs; run with zero data retention off.
